subject: Cloud Computing
title: Pay As You Go
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pay As You Go.

hook.text: You don't buy a power plant to charge your phone. Cloud works the same way — pay only for what you use.

buildup.text: Cloud providers charge by the second, hour, or gigabyte. No upfront cost, no long-term commitment required.

discovery.text: This model let startups launch for dollars instead of millions. No servers to buy, no data centers to build.

twist.text: Pay-as-you-go sounds cheap until usage spikes. An accidental loop can run up a $50,000 bill overnight.

climax.text: The model rewards efficiency. The more carefully you use resources, the less you pay.

punchline.text: Pay for what you use. But know what you're using.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of cloud pay-as-you-go pricing?
options: You only pay for the resources you actually consume
You pay a fixed monthly fee regardless of usage
Cloud providers charge based on company size

details.summary: Pay-as-you-go billing charges only for the cloud resources actually consumed, measured in seconds, hours, or API calls. It eliminates upfront capital expenditure and aligns cost with demand. This model enabled startups to launch without buying servers.
details.whyItMatters: Pay-as-you-go is the fundamental pricing innovation that made cloud computing accessible. It shifts IT spending from capital to operating expense, transforming how businesses budget for technology.
takeaways: You pay only for resources you actually consume
Costs scale linearly with actual usage

faq.question: How is pay-as-you-go measured?
faq.answer: Compute is typically billed per second or hour of instance runtime. Storage is billed per gigabyte-month. Data transfer is billed per gigabyte. API calls are billed per request or per million requests. Each service has its own metering unit.

faq.question: Is pay-as-you-go always the cheapest option?
faq.answer: No. For steady-state workloads, reserved instances or committed-use discounts are significantly cheaper. Pay-as-you-go is ideal for variable, unpredictable, or short-lived workloads where you cannot commit to long-term usage.
